subject: Request: side-by-side cost / latency inspector + SLA tags for tenant slices
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: side-by-side cost / latency inspector + SLA tags for tenant slices

Hi team,

Quick ask: Carolyn at ACME pinged last week asking for a single-pane view that lines up per-tenant cost (token spend / $) with latency tail stats (p95/p99) and SLA tagging so their SREs can quickly see which tenant slices are both expensive and close to SLOs.

Goal: a Console inspector panel that lets an operator pick a time window and a tenant slice and see:
- per-route cost breakdown (tokens, model variant, quantization)
- latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) side-by-side with cost columns
- SLA tag (green/amber/red) based on tenant-configured thresholds
- export CSV and a short permalink to share with customers

Why: current investigation flow requires running separate cost reports and latency queries; joining them is manual and blocks quick triage. ACME needs this for renewal discussions.

I've attached a quick mock (inspector-sketch-v2.png) and put a short spec in Notion: https://notion.redwood.com/console/inspector-side-by-side-v2. There's an open Jira: SUP-4822 that I started.

Asks:
- Engineering: feasibility + high level storage/compute constraints (sampling, pre-aggregation)
- Product: prioritization and UX owner for the widget
- Data: required metrics and any schema changes

Proposed owners: Marissa (product) + Soojin (eng) + Aditya (data) — open to changes.

Can everyone reply with quick feasibility notes? If feasible we should block a 30-min sync this week and decide a canary plan (internal-only first).

Thanks,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: inspector-sketch-v2.png

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: side-by-side cost / latency inspector + SLA tags for tenant slices

Thanks Vanessa — good summary. Quick engineering read:

Summary of constraints we need to surface:
1) Sampling vs full scan: high-cardinality tenant slices mean pre-aggregation is required for sub-hour windows; full per-request joins will be very expensive. We should define the smallest useful granularity and accept ~1-5 min lag.
2) Storage footprint: adding cost columns keyed by route x model_variant x tenant will increase OLAP footprint; we can avoid duplication if cost is stored as tokenized events with rollups.
3) Latency percentiles: we already have p50/p95/p99 histograms but joining histograms to token-level cost requires consistent time bucketing.
4) SLA tags: these are cheap if we only evaluate against existing p95/p99 thresholds, but needs a UI for tenant-level thresholds and a small control plane table.

Open questions:
- Sampling policy: do we allow a per-tenant sampling rate override? (Aditya?)
- Export format: CSV is fine, but do we need a more structured export (parquet) for deeper analysis?

Feasibility: Feasible as an MVP with pre-aggregated rollups (1m/5m buckets) and a small control-plane SLA table. Rough estimate: 3 sprints (eng + infra) for a canary (internal tenants only); additional sprint for export and shareable permalinks.

I'll sync with infra about storage cost and come back with capacity numbers.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Engineering Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: side-by-side cost / latency inspector + SLA tags for tenant slices

Appreciate the quick read, both. A few product notes and prioritization proposals:

1) Prioritization: put this in the "High" bin for Q3 because it directly affects renewal conversations for at least two seats (ACME + another enterprise prospect).

2) MVP scope (to keep cost modest):
- Single-pane table for tenant slices (tenant id, route, model variant) with columns: tokens, $ estimate, calls, p50, p95, p99, SLA status.
- Time window selector (15m/1h/24h) with auto-bucket suggestions.
- CSV export and a short permalink.
- Initial rollout: internal tenants -> opt-in early access for selected customers (ACME).

3) UX/Owner: I'll take UX ownership and produce a clickable mock by Friday. Vanessa, can you confirm whether ACME is fine with being in an opt-in beta? If yes, start the legal/engagement thread.

4) Metrics to capture for canary: token spend delta, average response time, p95/p99, query latency for the inspector itself. Aditya, please confirm exact metric names and whether any new rollups are required.

5) Rollout: canary (2 weeks) -> broader opt-in (4 weeks) -> GA. We'll validate that sampling/aggregation doesn't hide hotspots.

I'll schedule a 30-min triage tomorrow 11:00am PT; calendar invite incoming.

— Marissa
Product Lead, Console
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Request: side-by-side cost / latency inspector + SLA tags for tenant slices

Carolyn — following up from our call. We're greenlighting an internal canary for the side-by-side inspector; Marissa will own the UX and Soojin will lead eng. We want to invite ACME into an opt-in beta once we complete the internal canary (target: mid-July).

Two asks for you:
1) Confirm ACME is comfortable being an opt-in beta participant and sharing a handful of tenant ids (we'll need 3 example tenant slices).
2) Any non-negotiable columns you'd like in the first view? (we currently plan tokens/$, calls, p50/p95/p99, SLA status).

If you want to review the attached mock, Marissa will send the clickable shortly.

Thanks,
Vanessa
